page.layout: One column of running text; a centred italic subheading in the middle of the page; marginal notes at the lower right. Left-edge fragments belong to the neighbouring page and are not transcribed.

main_text.p: -civitate Attică donatus, discrimen certaminis in fese pro republicā & honore civitatis recepit, & cum provocante viribus fiso congressus, victoriaque nobili per fraudem potitus, dejecto Thymoete regnare jussus est. Atque ad hujus rei gestæ memoriam confervandam apaturiorum festum à populo institutum. Melantho regnāte Iones armis Achæorum in patria presti populariter ex Peloponneso Athenas venēre, & fatagente rege in jus civitatis admissi urbem agrumq; multitudine repleverunt. Melanthi filius Codrus patri suffectus cum bello Doriensi difficillimo pro salute reipublicæ morti se devovisset, in confertissimos hostes irruens & eorum telis se objiciens gloriose occubuit, regum Atticorum postremus. A morte enim ejus nomen regium, quod id libertati grave videretur, abrogatum.
main_text.head: Archontes Atheniensium perpetui.
main_text.p: Successori filio ejusdem Medontis, principis seu prætoris nomen datum, (ἄρχοντα Græci dicebant,) & cum novo nomine, quod magis secundum libertatem erat, potestas etiam diminuta, ut esset dedendis rationibus obnoxia, quemadmodum nos docet Pausanias[illegible, ~6 letters]

page.notes: Long s was rendered as plain s throughout. The subheading is set in italic and centred, so it is a level-2 heading. The Greek word ἄρχοντα is copied from the scan and may carry a printed accent I could not resolve; check it. "fiso" (line 3) is a doubtful reading: the scan shows a long-s form and the word may be "fiso" or a variant. "Peloponneso" is a doubtful spelling. The lower-right marginal figures (apparently Roman numerals, with a small ornament) are not legible enough to read reliably, so the note is marked illegible. The left-edge fragments belong to the neighbouring page and are excluded. No catchword is visible below the last line.
